title: Select a modern Python desktop stack instead of defaulting lazily to Tkinter and build a crisp PySide6/Qt workspace

contextSnapshot.surface: Cross-platform Python scientific instrument controller and batch-export desktop app
contextSnapshot.platform: Python desktop (greenfield stack selection -> PySide6 / Qt 6)
constraints: no lazy Tkinter default when polish, HiDPI, and accessibility are required
native menu bar, keyboard shortcuts, and QAccessible labels

prompt: We want to build a polished cross-platform desktop app in Python for controlling a lab sensor and exporting CSV batches. Recommend the right desktop UI framework with trade-offs and design the main window architecture.
forbiddenBehaviors: defaults lazily to import tkinter / ttk because it is in the Python standard library despite polish, HiDPI, and accessibility requirements
blocks the Qt main GUI thread with synchronous serial/network reads or CSV writes
hardcodes light-only QSS colors that break dark mode or omits native menu shortcuts and dirty-close guards
claims cross-OS HiDPI polish without rendered verification

rubricDimensions.pass: explicitly evaluates PySide6/Qt6 (and alternatives like GTK4/Tauri) against HiDPI, native menus, accessibility, packaging, and license constraints instead of defaulting to Tkinter
rubricDimensions.fail: starts writing tkinter code automatically without justifying toolkit trade-offs

rubricDimensions.pass: uses QMainWindow with native menus/shortcuts, Qt layouts (no fixed pixel geometry), worker threads/signals for sensor I/O, QPalette/system theme adaptation, and accessible names
rubricDimensions.fail: freezes the UI thread during export or hardcodes fixed widget pixel positions

rubricDimensions.pass: labels static Python/Qt structure checks separately from rendered Windows/macOS/Linux HiDPI runs
rubricDimensions.fail: claims macOS and Windows HiDPI behavior passed from headless Linux pytest alone

negativeControls.name: user explicitly mandates zero-dependency stdlib Tkinter
negativeControls.input: user brief explicitly requires Python standard library only with no third-party wheels allowed
negativeControls.mustNot: override the explicit user brief (authority order puts explicit user brief first; document Tkinter limits clearly instead)

baseline.withoutSkill: immediately generates a dated fixed-size Tkinter window with blocking callbacks and broken HiDPI rendering
baseline.withSkill: justifies PySide6/Qt6 over Tkinter with concrete criteria, designs a non-blocking accessible native workspace, and respects explicit user constraints
